text: The front desk said: "We're sold out."
That same night, their new room cost fourteen hundred dollars.
Nassau, the Bahamas. Kristine and Jimmy Dworkin, from California.
Night one of an eight-day trip: a Courtyard by Marriott. Prepaid.
At check-in... no room. The hotel was overbooked.
Kristine says the staff were "pretty rude about it."
Hotels often overbook on purpose: some guests never show up.
So around midnight, they walked the streets of Nassau.
One room left: a suite at Margaritaville.
Fourteen hundred dollars. For ONE night.
So they contacted NBC Bay Area.
A hospitality professor told NBC big hotels usually pay for your first night elsewhere.
Marriott's website, NBC found, only promises a new room... to elite members.
Then Marriott agreed to pay them back: the fourteen hundred, plus the original room.
In hotel slang, being sent to another hotel is called getting "walked."
Usually, the hotel arranges the walk. This time, the family did it... on foot.
